plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Daisy-like blooms with drooping rosy-purple petals surround a spiky, copper-orange central cone. Bees, butterflies and goldfinches crowd the prairie and garden stands in high summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer, roughly June through August, with some blooms from late spring and a possible second flush in early fall
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, in prairies, open woodlands and gardens
plants.funFact: The spiky central cone is a dense head of tiny individual flowers. Its seed heads feed finches through the autumn.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery, fragrant shrubs form rolling violet-blue stripes across sunbaked hillsides. The scent drifts on the warm summer air and draws clouds of bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to late August, peaking in July
plants.location: Provence and the French Alps, France
plants.funFact: Lavender has been prized since antiquity for its fragrance. The name is often traced to the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia
plants.description: Dense shrubs carry glowing orange-gold flower spikes that look like bottlebrushes. They light up the cool winter bushland and attract honeyeaters and lorikeets.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn through winter, generally March to August
plants.location: Coastal New South Wales, Australia, in sandy heathland
plants.funFact: Each spike is made up of thousands of tiny flowers. They produce so much nectar that birds and small mammals feed on it through the Australian winter.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest of the proteas, with a bowl-shaped flower head up to the size of a dinner plate. It has a crown of silky pink bracts and a fuzzy center, and it blooms against the winter backdrop of the Cape fynbos.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter and spring, mainly June to October
plants.location: Western Cape, South Africa, in fynbos and in gardens such as Kirstenbosch
plants.funFact: It is South Africa's national flower. The plant is adapted to fire, with a woody underground stem that resprouts after bushfires.
